column1: # Reader cases: records and collection files, nearly all in forms Banking4 never writes (cut short,
# malformed, or in an encoding its writer does not produce), and the expected result of reading
# Columns: id, kind (record|file), record_offset, record_size, buffer (hex), reads, expected.
# record: the record body is buffer[record_offset .. record_offset + record_size]; reads are applied in order.
# file:   buffer is a whole collection file; the reads are applied to every record.
# expected (record): 'open STATE | VALUE STATE | ...', one entry per read, ending early with ERR:corrupt
#   (corrupt stream) or ERR:fail (any other failure on reading). If the record cannot be opened
# expected (file): the records separated by ' || ', then EOF, ERR:corrupt, ERR:compat or ERR:fail.
# STATE is @cursor,chunk_start,chunk_end,more_chunks,consumed_size, positions relative to the record.
# VALUE: integers in decimal; true/false/null; decimal as [-]magnitude e-scale; strings as JSON
#   strings; blobs as x<hex>; date_raw as ymd(year,month,day)=>its conversion to a timestamp;
#   timestamps as ISO text with seven fractional digits, 'none' for the zero timestamp; time_hms
# A cursor near -2147483648 is a cursor that wrapped around on an absurd length
# In the short/ cases one valid value ends after 0..n of its bytes, with the chunk being the end of
# the record (last), followed by unused bytes (slack) or followed by another chunk (next).
